h: Before you bounce: a quick game plan
p: A bit of planning goes a long way with trampoline parks, and it makes the difference between a brilliant session and a frazzled one. First up, kit. Wear comfortable sportswear without zips, buckles or anything sharp, and leave jewellery and loose bits in the car or a locker. Long hair is best tied back. Grip socks are normally bought on your first visit and can be reused next time, so keep them safe once you've got them.

Arrive a little early. Checking in, sorting out waivers and getting everyone's socks on takes longer than you think, especially with a gang of excited kids, and you don't want to eat into your jump time. Most parks also run a short safety briefing, which is worth listening to properly: one person per trampoline is the golden rule, and it keeps everyone in one piece.

Pace yourselves. Even half an hour of jumping is a real workout, so take a breather and a drink between bursts of activity. Little ones may tire quickly, so a slot length that suits their age is a good shout.

Parents who'd rather watch than jump usually have a viewing area with somewhere to sit, and some parks have a café counter for a coffee. It's worth checking whether non-jumpers need to book or pay anything before you go.

Afterwards, Birmingham has plenty to fill the rest of your day. Cadbury World in Bournville is a hit with families, the National Sea Life Centre sits by the canals near Brindleyplace, and Cannon Hill Park is perfect for a calm wander once everyone's bounced out.
